sub_unit_name: Introduction - Classification of batteries- primary, secondary and reserve batteries with examples

content.title: What is a Battery?
content.description: A battery is an electrochemical device that converts stored chemical energy into electrical energy through oxidation-reduction (redox) reactions. It consists of one or more electrochemical cells connected together.

content.content: Batteries are widely used in electronic gadgets, automobiles, medical devices, defense equipment, and renewable energy systems. Based on their rechargeability and method of activation, batteries are classified into primary, secondary, and reserve batteries.

content.title: Importance of Batteries
content.content: Batteries provide portable, reliable, and uninterrupted power for various domestic, industrial, and military applications.
Primary batteries are non-rechargeable batteries. The chemical reactions occurring inside them are irreversible, and once the reactants are consumed, the battery cannot be reused.

content.title: Examples of Primary Batteries
content.description: Common examples include Dry Cell (Leclanché Cell), Alkaline Battery, Mercury Cell, and Zinc-Air Battery.

content.content: Secondary batteries are rechargeable batteries. Their chemical reactions are reversible, allowing them to be recharged by supplying external electrical energy after discharge.
Reserve batteries remain inactive until required. One of the reactants, usually the electrolyte, is stored separately and supplied only during operation. This gives the battery a long storage life.

content.title: Examples of Reserve Batteries
content.description: Lithium reserve batteries, magnesium reserve batteries, and thermal batteries are commonly used in missiles, spacecraft, and military equipment.

right_points: Suitable for repeated or emergency use

items.question: Primary Batteries
items.answer: Used in clocks, remote controls, flashlights, and toys.

items.question: Secondary Batteries
items.answer: Used in electric vehicles, laptops, UPS systems, and smartphones.

items.question: Reserve Batteries
items.answer: Used in missiles, satellites, life-saving equipment, and military communication systems.

items.question: Industrial Importance
items.answer: Batteries are essential for portable electronics, renewable energy storage, and backup power systems.

content.title: Key Point
content.content: Primary batteries are used once, secondary batteries can be recharged multiple times, and reserve batteries are activated only when required.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy.
Reserve batteries remain inactive until activated.
Battery selection depends on application, cost, and service life.
